phases.label: Follow the light
phases.title: A signal becomes a turn.
phases.caption: The angle to the light enters a real connectome. A trained decoder turns descending-neuron activity into steering.

phases.label: Meet the specimen
phases.title: Small body. Visible consequences.
phases.caption: Compound eyes, wing veins, bristles, six legs. The body and gait are illustrations; heading comes from neural output.

phases.label: Inside the network
phases.title: 166,700 neurons. In the loop.
phases.caption: These are recorded cell locations, including the ventral cord. Bright amber points are measured spike events, not decorative pulses.

phases.label: Windfall orchard
phases.title: Lunch is somewhere in the orchard.
phases.caption: Visit fallen-fruit patches. Each reward requires measured time near the food. Food-location and obstacle cues are engineered; neural activity still produces the turn.

phases.label: Follow the scent
phases.title: A scent trail. Not a straight line.
phases.caption: A simulated odor plume drifts downwind. Local concentration samples and a wind cue supply the bearing, without reading the food's direction. This is an engineered sensory adapter.

phases.label: Spider escape
phases.title: Eight legs. One urgent decision.
phases.caption: An engineered spider pursues the body. Threat proximity supplies an escape cue to the frozen neural controller. Contacts and exits from the danger zone are measured, not scripted victories.

phases.label: The dangerous picnic
phases.title: The food is good. The company isn't.
phases.caption: Forage between picnic scraps while a swatter crosses the table. The engineered adapter prioritizes escape when the threat is near. This is not retinal vision or natural decision-making.

phases.label: Between the stones
phases.title: Dinner. On the other side of the rubble.
phases.caption: Preselected route waypoints and short-range obstacle cues feed the same trained decoder through the real connectome. The route is engineered, not planned by the fly. Collision physics never manufactures a turn.

phases.label: Weather the gusts
phases.title: The world pushes back.
phases.caption: Gusts physically displace the body. Leaf shelters reduce that force. The neural controller responds to the changed position; these wind and shelter rules are illustrative, not validated biomechanics.

phases.label: The midnight porch
phases.title: Two warm lights. A very small traveler.
phases.caption: A moonlit porch replaces the laboratory. Visit both lamps using engineered location bearings. Atmospheric lighting is illustrative; it does not enter the brain as retinal pixels.

phases.label: Change the target
phases.title: Move the goal. Watch the response.
phases.caption: The light changes position every six numerical seconds. The same frozen network and decoder respond, without a fallback steering script.

phases.label: Reverse the task
phases.title: The same brain. A different task.
phases.caption: The engineered adapter reverses the desired bearing. The network and decoder stay unchanged while the body turns away.

phases.label: Brain-off control
phases.title: Take neural steering away.
phases.caption: Identical starting body and target. Neural activity and turn commands are suppressed. Forward speed remains, but heading cannot change.

phases.label: Restore neural output
phases.title: Put the network back in the loop.
phases.caption: Reset to the same starting body and target. Restore neural output. Watch steering return and the fly approach the light.

phases.label: Real wiring, honest limits
phases.title: Real wiring. Honest boundaries.
phases.caption: A simplified LIF reservoir with a trained task decoder. This does not establish innate phototaxis, consciousness, or an advantage over shuffled wiring.

phases.label: A closer look
phases.title: A little nervous system. Live.
phases.caption: The exhibit keeps running and repeats automatically. Every activity measurement comes from the live simulation.
